query: What open-response signals predict low learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: teacher_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Teacher responsiveness is a strong candidate signal for learning satisfaction, offering a clean grouping axis. Values are mostly grounded (ED-0003 'teacher can't tell when she's lost' -> slow/infrequent is reasonable), but some are stretched: ED-0004 has no evidence of any feedback yet is labeled 'responsive_with_rich_feedback', and ED-0002 gives no signal of feedback to students. These infer specifics the text is silent on.

per_column.name: instructional_mode_quality
per_column.rationale: Categorises delivery mode, a plausible driver of satisfaction. Labels largely align with text (ED-0004 pausable recorded lectures -> lecture_video_rewindable; ED-0002 creative adapted labs -> interactive_adaptive). 'mixed' is a safe default for silent rows and not overreaching.

per_column.name: student_engagement_signal
per_column.rationale: Engagement is a central, directly relevant axis for satisfaction analysis. Values track evidence well (ED-0005 cameras off/muted -> disengaged_cameras_off; ED-0001 avoidance -> disengaged_avoidance_behavior). ED-0001 'disengaged_avoidance_behavior' is a slight stretch from technical frustration but defensible.

per_column.name: subject_format_fit
per_column.rationale: Whether a subject adapts to online format is a genuine analytical lever and interacts with the 'subject' column. Labels are well warranted (ED-0002 kitchen-chemistry works -> well_adapted; ED-0001 algebra whiteboard fails -> poorly_adapted).

per_column.name: peer_interaction_loss
per_column.rationale: Peer-interaction loss is a meaningful, distinct satisfaction signal with graded categories. Mostly grounded (ED-0003 'zero peer interaction' -> severe; 'not_present' for silent rows is correct). ED-0005 labeled 'severe_loss_community_absent' overreads a teacher's complaint about silent students into a community-loss claim not clearly stated.

judge.rationale: All five added columns provide distinct, non-redundant categorical axes (responsiveness, mode, engagement, subject fit, peer loss) that are each directly relevant to predicting low learning satisfaction, giving strong grouping/modeling leverage for the query. None are near-constant or trivial restatements. Groundedness is generally solid: most values are sound readings of the source text and silent rows default to reasonable 'not_present' labels. The main weaknesses are occasional over-specific inferences—teacher_responsiveness asserting 'rich feedback' where the text is silent, and peer_interaction_loss escalating to 'severe' on thin evidence—but these are localized rather than systemic.
